title: Counselling
description: Provides counselling and psychotherapy to individuals, couples and families facing interpersonal, intrapersonal, and mental health issues.

sections.About this support:
**Counselling and therapy services include:**

- Family Therapy
- Couple/Marital Therapy
- Individual Psychotherapy
- Pre-marital counselling and marriage preparation
- Counselling on sexuality and sexual issues
- Counselling and therapy sessions can be conducted in-person or online via Zoom.

**Helplines:**

- Care Corner Counselling Centre also runs a toll-free Mandarin Counselling Hotline at 1800 353 5800 daily from 10am to 10pm, excluding public holidays.
- SAMH Insight Centre also provides a toll-free helpline at 1800 287 7019 (9am to 6pm on weekdays, except 1pm to 2pm and public holidays).
sections.Who is this for?:
Individuals, couples and families with issues such as:

- Marital and relationship issues
- Family and parenting issues
- Grief and loss
- Mental health
- Personal challenges
- Stress
- Trauma
sections.How to apply?: For enquiries or appointment booking, call or email the respective service provider.
sections.What to expect?:
- The service provider will assess the request for counselling and ask your presenting issues and preferred day/time for the counselling and arrange a slot for you accordingly.
- The staff will also provide information on the fees.
- Counselling intake and assessment is conducted at the first appointment and the client will see the same counsellor for the subsequent sessions until the case is closed or transferred.
- If counselling is not suitable, the counsellor may refer you to other appropriate services.
- A counselling session takes around 1 hour.
- Most issues will need more than 1 counselling session to resolve.
- Fees payable for all service providers except SAMH Insight Centre.

title: Counselling (Seniors)
description: Provides counselling to older persons aged 50 and above and/or their caregivers, to improve their mental well-being and resilience to cope with life’s challenges.

sections.About this support:
- Gerontological counselling provides an avenue for seniors and their caregivers to discuss their issues and concerns and help to address their personal, social or psychological challenges.
- Individual and group counselling available.
- Counselling can be provided at the counselling centre or at their own home if necessary.
sections.Who is this for?:
Persons aged 50 years old and above with issues and concerns such as:

- Grief and loss
- Loneliness/isolation
- Depression
- Stress and anxiety
- Relationship problems
- Difficulty adjusting to transitions and changes (e.g. retirement, ‘empty nest’ syndrome, onset of illnesses)

Family members/caregivers who experience stress caring for their elderly loved ones who are experiencing the above-mentioned concerns can also be supported.

Hua Mei Centre for Successful Ageing also provides individual and group coaching in emotion management, inter-generational relationship-building and communication skills.
sections.How to apply?: For enquiries or appointment booking, call or email the respective service provider.
sections.What to expect?:
- The counselling centre will arrange an appointment for you with a professional counsellor who will assess your needs and advise if counselling is able to meet your needs.
- If counselling is not suitable, the counsellor will refer you to other appropriate services.
- A counselling session takes around 1 to 1.5 hours.
- Most issues will need more than 1 counselling session to resolve.
- Fees payable for Hua Mei Centre for Successful Ageing and O’Joy Limited.

title: Medical Fee Exemption Card (MFEC)
description: Subsidised standard medical treatment for needy residents at approved stay-in care institutions.
highlights: Subsidies standard medical care for eligible stay-in care recipients

sections.About this support: Provides subsidised standard medical treatment for eligible stay-in care recipients at government or restructured hospitals, polyclinics and approved Community Care Services.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen (SC), Permanent Resident (PR) or stateless person with valid ICA documentation
- Subsidised resident living in an approved MOH-funded institutions
- Must meet the means-test criteria for MFEC
sections.How to apply?: You can approach the medical social worker in the institution your loved one is staying in. They will help your loved one to apply for the card.
sections.Where to go: [Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)
sections.Phone number:
AIC hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060)

Calls from the AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

title: Live On!
description: Year-long, family-centric psychological intervention for youths with high suicide risk as they transit from hospitalisation into the community.

sections.About this support:
- LiveOn! is a 1-year high frequency and intensive suicide intervention programme that targets youths aged 12 to 18 years old with suicidality risk, and includes their family members in the intervention.
- Objectives of the programme includes:
  - Providing immediate support to youths with suicidal thoughts or attempts in the community
  - Providing continuous community support for youths and the families once they are discharged from primary care institutions
  - De-escalating youths' emotions and strengthening family support through individual and family counselling
sections.Who is this for?: - 12 to 18 years old youths who have been discharged from IMH due to suicidality.
sections.How to apply?:
- This programme is only eligible for youths who have been discharged by IMH, KKH, NUH, and other public hospitals due to suicidality, and have been assessed by a clinician to be eligible for referral.
- Call the TOUCHline (1800 377 2252, 9am to 6pm from Monday to Friday) or email [mentalhealth@touch.org.sg](mailto:mentalhealth@touch.org.sg) if you do not have a hospital referral but still require support.
- If you are suicidal and require immediate support, call Samaritans of Singapore (SOS) at 1767.
sections.What to expect?:
This programme consists of individual counselling for the youths, as well as family sessions.

**Individual sessions (for the youth)**

- In the Acute phase, the youth will meet with the social worker / counsellor / psychologist weekly for 6 to 12 sessions to de-escalate emotions.
- In the Continuation phase, the youth will meet with the social worker / counsellor / psychologist twice a month, for another 5 to 12 sessions.
- In the Maintenance phase after the above is completed, the youth will remain in contact with the caseworker through calls and text messages for 3 to 6 months for continuous support and monitoring . If youths relapse, an assessment will be conducted and the case will be re-opened.

**Family sessions (for the caregivers of the youth)**

- Meet with the social worker / counsellor twice a month from the start of the programme for 4 to 6 sessions to learn skills on how to support the youth better, which includes safety planning and crisis management School counsellors will also be contacted, with client and parental consent.

title: Safe Place
description: Programme aims to empower women and their families with unsupported pregnancies to make informed and life-giving choices.

sections.About this support:
The programme provides the following services:

- Case management and counselling
- Pre- and postnatal skills equipping
- Baby essentials
- Temporary accommodation
- Referrals to other support partners
sections.Who is this for?: Safe Place serves pregnant women up to 32 weeks gestation who consent to receiving support services. For clients under 17 years, parental consent is required, although exceptions are considered based on individual circumstances.
sections.How to apply?:
If you are a pregnant woman who needs help, know of one who needs help or need information about unsupported pregnancy, please contact Safe Place at 6817 4202 or text via WhatsApp at 8891 4214 to speak to the caseworkers.

For community partners, please submit a referral form and attach a social report (if available) via email ([safeplace@lakeside.org.sg](mailto:safeplace@lakeside.org.sg)).

A social worker will be in touch within 3 working days.
sections.What to expect?:
Service users who require help with their pregnancy may contact Safe Place via email/call/WhatsApp.

Case plans and duration of case are customised to meet the unique needs and circumstances of the service users.

title: grovve
description: An integrated, youth-centric wellness centre offering a safe space where young people aged 12 to 25 can seek mental health support.

sections.About this support:
- A welcoming space where youths aged 12 to 25 can hang out and access mental health support.
- An on-site concierge manages basic support needs for youths and their caregivers.
- For those requiring more in-depth support such as counselling or case management, a range of services are available through on-site partner organisations.
- Scheduled activities are also organised within the space to engage youths and caregivers.
sections.Who is this for?: Youths aged 12 to 25 and their caregivers
sections.How to apply?: Walk in during opening hours or get in touch with grovve via WhatsApp at https://mindline.sg/grovve/about/visit.
sections.What to expect?:
Youths can drop by Grovve anytime during opening hours and speak to a concierge staff member.

- Staff will take time to get to know each youth better, whether through conversation or questionnaires, to understand how best to support them.
- Where further support is needed, youths and their caregivers may be referred to the relevant on-site partner organisations.

title: Healthy with KIDSTART
description: Support lower income families with Singapore Citizen children aged up to 6 years old with fresh produce packs.

sections.About this support:
Healthy with KidSTART was designed intentially to plug the intersection of early childhood nutritional needs and to support families with doorstep delivery to alleviate the logistical stress. Fresh produce packs will be delivered monthly to onboard KidSTART families to:

- Introduce to parents the importance of early childhood nutrition and impact their desire to establish good and healthy eating habits in their children from young.
- Seed the appreciation of a variety of healthy produce early for children and encourage future healthy eating habits.
- Improve accessibility of fresh produce for onboarded families of fresh produce for onboarded families.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen children aged up to 6 years old
- Low-income household (i.e., household income of <= $2,500 or per capital monthly income of <=$650)The Healthy with KidSTART programme is for KidSTART families only. If interested in the programme, please enquire with  KidSTART practitioners on how you can sign up for the programme.
sections.How to apply?: The Healthy with KidSTART programme is for KidSTART families only. If interested in the programme, please enquire with KidSTART practitioners on how you can sign up for the programme.
sections.What to expect?:
- Fresh produce packs filled with fresh fruits and vegetables
- Recipe cards featuring nutritious dishes that are easy to prepare for the entire family
- Invitation to cooking demonstration workshops by celebrity chefs and events
- Healthy plate that guides you to prepare better portioned meals for your children

title: Sober Living Framework (SLF)
description: Provides crisis intervention, therapy support, and long-term aftercare for persons and families impacted by substance and/or behavioural addictions.

sections.About this support:
The SLF comprises intervention tracks for addicted persons or Significant Other Persons (SOP; includes kin and family members, partner, close friends, guardian) at 5 different stages of needs:

- Track 1: Outreach, Education and Awareness – to raise awareness of addictions and advocate for early intervention
- Track 2: Relapse Prevention and Extended Care – individual and group counselling, family support, self-help support group
- Track 3: Sober Living – for persons in the early remission phase with less than 6 months sobriety from addictive behaviour
- Track 4: Maintenance – for persons with at least 6 months sobriety
- Track 5: For Family/SOP – individual and group counselling, support group

Note: Not all participants will enter and complete each track in a linear order.
sections.Who is this for?:
All services are open to Singapore Citizens and persons residing in Singapore who are:

- Assessed to have a present or past addiction issue (including drugs, alcohol, compulsive gambling, shoplifting, sex, porn use and gaming), with the expressed desire to seek help or,
- Currently impacted by the addiction of a loved one.

For addiction treatment:

- Services are provided to all persons aged 14 and above

For family counselling:

- Support is provided to individuals aged 10 and above

For outreach programmes:

- Conducted for individuals aged 14 and above

Those who are under the age of 16 must be accompanied by a parent, guardian or authorised adult.
sections.How to apply?: You may contact WE CARE for more information. Alternatively, WE CARE also accepts referrals through other agencies (e.g. State Courts, MSF, Prisons, family service centres, hospitals, other social service agencies).
sections.What to expect?:
The intake and assessment process involves an interview where the person’s motivation is assessed and their readiness, reasons and desire for change are explored.

- For persons who are assessed to be ambivalent about stopping their addictive behaviour, brief therapy will be conducted, with the primary goal of engaging with the person such that they will return for help in the future when ready for change.
- For persons who are assessed to be highly motivated for change, they will be recommended to seek medical detoxification (if necessary), or directly assigned to the relevant track.

title: Maintenance Support Central (MSC)
description: Provides support and assistance for clients who have difficulty in receiving spousal and/or child maintenance.

sections.About this support:
MSC empowers individuals by providing knowledge of their marital and maintenance rights while offering comprehensive support in collaboration with community partners.

1.      Maintenance Applications

- Assists in the filing of Fresh Maintenance Applications (FMO) via the Integrated Family Application Management System (iFAMS)
- Assists in the Enforcement of Maintenance Orders (EMO) through video-link filing (iFAMS)
- Appointments must be made in advance

2.      Legal Clinics

- Offers Civil Family Law legal clinic on the first and third Monday evenings of each month
- Offers Syariah Family Law legal clinic on the third Monday of each month
- Legal clinics are open to individuals residing in Singapore, with an income cap criteria

3.      Court Process Guidance

- Offers legal guidance which includes explanation of standard legal procedures and legal terms related to family law

4.      Counselling Services

- Provides face-to-face and phone counselling for individuals who require emotional support for marital issues, post-divorce/separations, parenthood struggles, and/or similar concerns
- Counselling services are chargeable, based on clients’ financial capabilities

5.      Educational Talks

- Legal talks on family law matters designed to benefit the public, social service professionals, and community partners. These sessions aim to raise awareness, enhance understanding, and equip participants with practical knowledge to navigate legal challenges effectively.
- Talks are conducted by guest speakers who are experts in Family and Syariah law

MSC also assists in responding to enquiries by sharing information or referring them to other community partners.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Services are rendered to individuals residing in Singapore who face financial abuse, marital issues, or have a Singapore court order and require legal support to navigate family law matters.
- This includes individuals who are dealing with unpaid maintenance, divorce proceedings, and financial difficulties arising from marital conflicts.
sections.How to apply?:
- You may apply to file Fresh or Enforcement of Maintenance application online (https://ifams.gov.sg/sop/#iFAMS). Alternatively, you may also contact the MSC programme's hotline at 6837 0611 to make an appointment.
- You can register for the online legal clinic (https://forms.office.com/r/4JucwmuQfc). If you qualify, programme staff will get back to you by 3 working days on the details.
- You may register for counselling service online (https://forms.office.com/r/mvdxTJcBFF) or call the hotline at 6571 0185 / 6837 0611 (WhatsApp)
sections.What to expect?: Service users who require the programme’s services will need to complete a registration form. Staff will confirm the appointments with the service user within 3 to 5 working days of form submission. For clients who register for legal clinic or counselling service, the processing time is 3 working days. All other services can be arranged at the time of contact.

title: Addiction Support Programme for Inclusion, Recovery, and Empowerment (ASPIRE)
description: For individuals aged 10 and above who have a present or past addiction issue (including gaming, compulsive gambling, shoplifting, drugs, alcohol, sex and porn use) or are currently impacted by the addiction of a loved one.

sections.About this support: Addiction Support Programme for Inclusion, Recovery and Empowerment (ASPIRE) provides screening, intake, assessment, and intervention, for persons and families impacted by addictions, particularly behavioural addictions. It provides professional community therapeutic services that contributes to the community integration of persons and families affected by addictions.
sections.Who is this for?:
Singapore citizens and persons residing in Singapore who are:

1. assessed to have a present or past addiction issue (including gaming, compulsive gambling, shoplifting, drugs, alcohol, sex and porn use), with the expressed desire to seek help OR
2. currently impacted by the addiction of a loved one.
sections.How to apply?: You may call, walk-in, or email our various agencies for requests on counselling. You may also be referred from other organisations and services. Information about the Addiction Support Service is available via the agencies’ website and brochures.
sections.What to expect?: Individuals who seek help can expect in-person and virtual counselling. These can take place via individual sessions, family sessions or group sessions. If referred, individuals are screened for service eligibility within 3 weeks after case is allocated/assigned.

title: Babes Pregnancy Crisis Support
description: For individuals aged 21 and below needing support with their pregnancy, so that they are aware of their options and are able to make an informed decision regarding their pregnancy.

sections.About this support:
Babes supports pregnant teens through:

- Casework and counselling
- 24-hour helpline
- Practical support (befriender, baby essentials, employment & back to school assistance etc)
- Information & resources
- Outreach and youth engagement events
sections.Who is this for?:
- Pregnant teenager who needs help; Anyone who needs information about teenage pregnancy
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
sections.How to apply?: If you are a pregnant teen who needs help, know of one who needs help or need information about teenage pregnancy, please contact Babes' 24-hour helpline at 6206 6641 or text via WhatsApp at 8111 3535 to speak to the caseworkers.
sections.What to expect?:
- Teenagers who require help with their pregnancy and/or anyone who needs information about teenage pregnancy may contact Babes via the 24-hour helpline (call/text).
- When an enquiry is attended to, the Helpliner will also assess if the teenager is eligible to be a case under Babes. Should the assessment be one that Babes can assist, Babes will arrange for a meeting with the teenager and/or her family/partner within 3-5 working days to assess the needs and provide the necessary support and guidance.

title: Protection Specialist Centre (PSC)
description: Provides services for individuals and families experiencing family violence, intimate partner violence or sexual violence.

sections.About this support:
Protection Specialist Centres (PSC) provide a holistic range of socio-emotional, supportive and practical services to survivors, including their families and other vulnerable members in the family in order to address the danger and likelihood of future harm posed to the survivors and meet the survivors’ needs.

Services provided include:

- Casework
- Counselling
- Application of personal protection orders
sections.Who is this for?:
- Survivors of family violence, intimate partner violence or sexual violence
- Persons who abuse
- Vulnerable family members who are witnesses of abuse or neglect/self-neglect.
sections.How to apply?:
You may refer to the Service Providers section and call or email any of the centres for assistance.

**Care Corner Project StART** 
[6476 1482](tel:64761482)
[projectstart@carecorner.org.sg](mailto:projectstart@carecorner.org.sg) 
[Website](https://www.carecorner.org.sg/family-violence-protection)

**TRANS SAFE Centre** 
[64499088](tel:64499088) 
[transsafe@trans.org.sg](mailto:transsafe@trans.org.sg) 
[Website](https://www.trans.org.sg/services/family-violence-protection-sexual-violence-recovery/)

**PAVE Integrated Services for Individual and Family Protection Specialist Centre (ISIFPSC)** 
For both family violence and child protection 
[65550390](tel:65550390) 
[intake@pave.org.sg](mailto:intake@pave.org.sg) 
[Website](https://www.pave.org.sg)
sections.What to expect?:
- Clients who approach or are referred to the centres will undergo an interview where caseworkers will assess the client’s needs.
- Appropriate information, referral and/or services will then be provided.

title: Community Mental Health Services
description: Community mental health teams located across Singapore provide support and access to mental health care for those in need.

sections.About this support: Mental health support services are offered by over 100 community mental health teams islandwide, with at least 1 team in every neighbourhood. These teams serve as the first stop for in-person mental health support.
sections.Who is this for?: Anyone aged 12 and above, and in need of mental health support.
sections.How to apply?:
- Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Community-Mental-Health-Services) to search for service providers by** **postal code, address or your device’s current location.
- Contact the team directly for an appointment.

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.
sections.What to expect?:
- Every visit is strictly confidential.
- Trained care professionals in each team will help identify your needs, develop a personalised care plan and provide support such as counselling and therapy.
- They can also help to escalate and make necessary referrals if needed.

title: SOS Suicide Crisis Intervention Programme
description: Provides confidential emotional support to individuals facing a crisis, thinking about suicide or affected by suicide through helpline, face to face in-person, and other support services.

sections.About this support:
SOS Suicide Crisis Intervention Programme comprises:

- 24-hour Hotline
- CareText
- Intervention outcalls
- Specialist counselling for individuals in crisis and persons grieving a suicide loss
- Support groups for individuals with prior suicide attempts and active suicidality
- The Programme serves self-referrals, as well as referrals from partner agencies (i.e. police, hospitals, social service agencies) and concerned third parties.
sections.Who is this for?: Persons at risk of suicide
sections.How to apply?: Reach out to SOS via the 24/7 Hotline: 1767; or CareText: WhatsApp 9151 1767.
sections.What to expect?: Clients can access SOS Hotline calling 1767, a 24-hour Hotline run by trained volunteers and staff. Depending on suicide risk, clients may be encouraged to seek immediate support from the hospitals (e.g. IMH), and/or receive community services or further counselling support at SOS. For callers with immediate suicide risk, SOS will activate their mobile crisis response team ("Active Rescue") to coordinate and deliver emergency intervention, led by a Crisis Support Supervisor on duty.

title: Lighthouse Project
description: Provides psychotherapy, psychological assessment and case management for youths aged 12–25 with complex moderate to high mental health needs.

sections.About this support:
The Lighthouse Project aims to be a beacon of light that attracts and correctly directs youths (aged 12-25 years old) with complex moderate to high mental health needs to accessible and appropriate help by doing the following:

- Provides psychotherapy (e.g. cognitive behavioural therapy) for youths with complex moderate to high mental health needs.
- Conducts psychological assessments (e.g. UCLA PTSD scale) to evaluate and monitor clients.
- Provides case management including referral to hospitals, case conferencing, and handholding into hospital-based treatment.
- Right-sites youths requiring higher-tiered care into primary, secondary, or tertiary care using the therapeutic relationship built with Limitless practitioners.
- Improves community standards of care through clinical supervision and training of partner organisations by Limitless' psychologists.
sections.Who is this for?: Youths aged 12-25 with moderate to high mental health needs.
sections.How to apply?:
Clients need to be referred by service providers or restructured hospitals. Self-referrals are also accepted and assessed for eligibility.

Contact Limitless at *SCAPE, 2 Orchard Link, #04-06 grovve, Singapore 237978. Operating hours: Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm.
sections.What to expect?: Clients would need to be referred to the programme. Lighthouse project staff would then make contact with the youth for assessment and basic emotional support. Youths may then be referred further. The duration and frequency of sessions would depend on clinician assessment.

title: Local Outreach to Suicide Survivors (LOSS)
description: LOSS provides immediate and long-term emotional support to persons who have lost a loved one or someone they knew to suicide ("suicide survivors"), primarily through support groups, texts, phone calls, and counselling sessions.

sections.About this support:
LOSS serves persons grieving a suicide loss, who include self-referrals, referrals from police, healthcare, and community partners, and concerned third parties.

It comprises:

- Support groups for persons grieving a suicide loss, facilitated by SOS grief counselling specialists and trained volunteers with lived experience ("Healing Companions").
- Additional emotional support through phone calls, text, and counselling sessions (where appropriate).
sections.Who is this for?: Persons grieving a suicide loss
sections.How to apply?: Reach out to SOS via the 24/7 Hotline: 1767; or CareText: WhatsApp 91511767.
sections.What to expect?: - When you reach out to SOS via call, text or email, SOS staff or trained volunteers will provide emotional support and if needed, encourage you to come for grief counselling and attend support groups subsequently for longer term support.

title: Community Law Centre in North West (Community Law Centre @ Realm of Tranquility)
description: This programme seeks to deliver integrated legal care in the North West District of Singapore by working collaboratively with community partners to holistically help and empower socially excluded individuals.

sections.Who is this for?:
The key target groups that the programme intends to serve include:

1. Socially excluded persons* residing or working in the North West District (based on CDC postal locator) who face legal and other complex issues, and who will benefit from integrated legal care; and
2. Community partners such as Family Service Centres, Community Development Councils, Social Service Offices and Social Service Agencies in the North West District.

*Socially excluded persons are persons who may face significant barriers in accessing legal services due to socio-economic, mobility, psychological, psychiatric, language and technological factors. Such persons may include transnational families and the sandwich class who do not qualify for Government legal aid schemes.
sections.How to apply?:
Members of the public and community partners may contact the Community Law Centre @ Realm of Tranquility through the following modes:

- Address: Community Law Centre @ Realm of Tranquility, Blk 547, Woodlands Dr 16, #01-177, Singapore 730547
- Email: [help@probono.sg](mailto:help@probono.sg)
- Hotline: 6536 0650
- Office operating hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00 am – 12:00 pm and 2:00 pm – 5:00 pm. Closed on weekends and public holidays.
- Hotline operating hours: Monday to Friday, 10:00 am – 1:00 pm and 2:00 pm – 4:00 pm. Closed on weekends and public holiday
sections.What to expect?:
Members of the public and community partners may contact the Community Law Centre @ Realm of Tranquility through the following modes:

- Address: Community Law Centre @ Realm of Tranquility, Blk 547, Woodlands Dr 16, #01-177, Singapore 730547
- Email: [help@probono.sg](mailto:help@probono.sg)
- Hotline: 6536 0650
- Office operating hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00 am – 12:00 pm and 2:00 pm – 5:00 pm. Closed on weekends and public holidays.
- Hotline operating hours: Monday to Friday, 10:00 am – 1:00 pm and 2:00 pm – 4:00 pm. Closed on weekends and public holiday

title: SOS Care Text
description: 24/7 confidential text support for suicide prevention and crisis intervention, accessible to all but targeting at youths from the ages 10 to 29 years old with suicide risk.

sections.About this support:
Samaritans of Singapore (SOS) Care Text is dedicated to providing confidential emotional support to individuals facing a crisis, thinking about suicide or affected by suicide. This crisis intervention and suicide prevention work is done through text messaging.

This programme contributes to the identification of individuals who are suicidal or in crisis, initiation of early intervention and preventive measures, and connecting these individuals to appropriate resources where necessary

This programme is targeted at youths from the ages of 10 to 29 years old with suicide risk, but not limited to this group and anyone can access this service. Programme aims to reduce suicide risks for persons in distress through texting which is a preference for the youths. The SOS Care Text is available round-the-clock to anyone who requires emotional support and or is affected by suicide and complements the current SOS crisis hotline service. The text service is anonymous.
sections.Who is this for?: Targeted at youths aged 10 to 29 years old with suicide risk, but services are open to all users.
sections.How to apply?: CareText can be accessed via WhatsApp at 9151 1767.
sections.What to expect?: Clients can access CareText by texting in to WhatsApp 9151 1767. The 24-hour text messaging platform run by trained volunteers and professional staff. Depending on users' needs, they may be encouraged to seek immediate support from the hospitals (e.g. IMH), and/or receive community services or further counselling support at SOS. For texters with immediate suicide risk, SOS will activate their mobile crisis response team ("Active Rescue") to coordinate and deliver emergency intervention, led by a Crisis Support Supervisor on duty.

title: WiShine
description: This programme seeks to support widows and their children who are in bereavement, especially in the widow’s initial adjustment to widowhood. It also supports widows who have relapsed into their grief and have difficulty coping with grief and have weak social support.

sections.About this support:
There are 5 core services for Widows:

a) Individual Grief Counselling

b) Peer Support Groups known as Care and Connect Groups

c) Befriending

d) Community Building Activities

e) Information & Referral

There are 4 core services for the Fatherless:

a) Grief Counselling

b) Integrated Talk & Arts Therapy

c) Home Based Therapy Sessions

d) Peer support group for children below 13 years old
sections.Who is this for?: Widows and their children with bereavement issues who require social and emotional support.
sections.How to apply?: You may call 6354 2475 or email [wishine@wicare.org.sg](mailto:wishine@wicare.org.sg) to apply.
sections.What to expect?:
a) Contact the centre to sign up for the programme.

b) The centre will contact you to confirm your registration.

title: SAMH Youthreach
description: Provides psychosocial support and recovery programmes for youths aged 13 to 21 with emotional, psychological and psychiatric issues in the community.

sections.About this support:
The programme staff work with youths and their families to minimise risk, promote safety and improve functioning.

Services include:

- Counselling Case Management
- Family Psychoeducation Programme
- Expressive Therapies
- Psycho-social Activities
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents aged 13 to 21 with emotional, psychological and/or psychiatric issues.
- No recent history of violent behaviour, alcohol or substance abuse, or sexual acting out behaviour.
- Willing to participate in the centre's activities.
- Family is willing to participate in case management and family education programmes.
sections.How to apply?: Referral by a psychiatrist, school counsellor, or social worker using the SAMH referral form is required.
sections.What to expect?:
- An intake interview with child/youth and caregiver will be arranged to assess suitability.
- Upon successful registration, the child/youth and caregiver will be engaged for services including case management, psychoeducation and psychosocial development programmes.

title: Community Outreach Teams (CREST)
description: Listens to your concerns and provides support such as therapy, as your in-person First Stop for Mental Health.

sections.About this support:
You can approach over 100 community mental health teams in the community islandwide such as CREST, providing the following support:

- Promote early recognition of signs and symptoms of mental health conditions and/or dementia.
- Improve mental health conditions and/or dementia literacy by organising targeted outreach events and activities to provide mental health and/or dementia information and education to residents and caregivers in the region.
- Provide psychosocial intervention such as techniques to reduce the risk of escalation of mental health needs.
- Provide collaborative and coordinated care for clients and caregivers through a case management approach.
- Work in partnership with health and community care partners and key stakeholders to co-manage and support persons with mental health conditions and dementia in the community.

These community mental health teams are developed under the Community Mental Health Masterplan driven by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), together with the Ministry of Health (MOH). The teams are fully funded by the government and there is no out-of-pocket cost.
sections.Who is this for?:
Any individual who is:

- At risk of mental health conditions and/or dementia, and their caregivers
- Aged 18 and above
sections.How to apply?:
- Call or email the providers to make an appointment. Visit [AIC’s website](https://aic.sg/Care-Services/Community-Mental-Health-Services) to search for service providers by** **postal code, address or your device’s current location.
- If you are already seeing a General Practitioner (GP) or Polyclinic doctor, you may approach them for support.
sections.What to expect?: - Applicants may need to fulfil the services’ in-take criteria and providers’ service boundaries, if any.

title: Youth Integrated Team (YIT)
description: Provides community-based mental health assessment, therapeutic intervention, case management for youths with mild mental health conditions while monitoring and checking in with the youth before, during and after intervention has been provided.

sections.About this support:
You can approach over 100 community mental health teams in the community islandwide such as YIT, providing the following support:

- Provide mental health assessments and support youths in understanding and identifying their care needs.
- Provide coordinated person-centric care intervention and support for youths and their caregivers through providing assessments, therapeutic intervention and case management.
- Engage community and healthcare partners to build a supportive environment for youths with mental health conditions through active collaboration and co-management of cases.
- Facilitate the formation of supportive relationships with families and peers in the recovery journey of youths.

These community mental health teams are developed under the Community Mental Health Masterplan driven by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), together with the Ministry of Health (MOH). The teams are fully funded by the government and there is no out-of-pocket cost.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Youths at higher risk for mental health conditions, their families and their support systems.
- Aged 12 to 25 years old
sections.How to apply?:
- Call or email the providers to make an appointment. Visit [AIC’s website](https://aic.sg/Care-Services/Community-Mental-Health-Services) to search for service providers by** **postal code, address or your device’s current location.
- If you are already seeing a General Practitioner (GP) or Polyclinic doctor, you may approach them for support.
sections.What to expect?: Applicants may need to fulfil the services’ in-take criteria and providers’ service boundaries, if any.

title: Strengthening Families Programme (FAM)
description: Provides divorce support and family counselling to all families.

sections.About this support:
- Provides specialised services and programmes for families facing early signs of stress, as well as divorcing and divorced families.
- These support services include marriage and divorce support programmes, and a family counselling service.
- For Minor couples who are marrying, they are required to attend a complimentary mandatory Marriage Preparation Programme (MPrep - required by law) provided by the agency.
- Young couples are also encouraged to attend the MPrep before they marry.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Divorcing and divorced families
- Families facing marital, parenting or intrapersonal issues
- Individuals/couples below 21 years old need to seek parental or guardian (who is above 21 years old) consent.
- Strengthening Families Programme (Fei Yue - Choa Chu Kang) and Strengthening Families Programme (Care Corner - Tampines) also provide marriage support for civil minor couples (either one or both parties under 18 years old), civil young couples (groom aged between 21 and 24, bride 21 & above), and transnational couples
sections.How to apply?: Apply through phone calls, emails, walk-in, or referrals by other agencies.
sections.What to expect?:
- Individuals/couples can contact the agency to request for more information on services.
- Agency worker will conduct an enquiry and intake assessment for suitability and appropriate services required.

title: Transitional Shelter (TS)
description: Provide temporary accommodation and social work intervention to homeless families who have exhausted all other means of accommodation.

sections.About this support:
- Transitional Shelter (TS) provides temporary accommodation to homeless families who have exhausted all other means of accommodation.
- It provides onsite social work intervention to address the complex needs of the admitted families/individuals to achieve long-term and stable housing.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen/ Permanent Resident
- Exhausted all other means of accommodation and facing financial difficulties
- Require social work intervention and willing to work with caseworkers to achieve long-term housing
- Able to live independently in the community, in a communal shelter setting (i.e. does not require close supervision or nursing care)
sections.How to apply?:
- You may contact your nearest Family Service Centre (FSC) for assistance if you are homeless.
- The TS will only accept applications from FSCs and other community agencies with social work competencies that can assess whether the family/individual meets the admission criteria.
- The referring agency will need to send in the application form, social report and supporting documents to TS for assessment.

To find the FSC in your neighbourhood, call Comcare hotline at [1800 222 0000](tel:18002220000) or visit 
https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories.
sections.What to expect?:
- Upon receiving referral, the TS will conduct an intake assessment to ensure that the applicant is eligible for the shelter.
- Clients must work with the TS on case goals and intervention plans to achieve long-term stable housing eventually.

title: Child Protection Specialist Centre (CPSC)
description: Serves as specialists on child protection matters to provide community-based support to children who face abuse or neglect at home.

sections.About this support:
Child Protection Specialist Centres (CPSCs) provide child-centric, family-focused and community-based support to children who face abuse or neglect at home.

Support provided includes:

- Safety planning
- Casework intervention
- Counselling to address the risks posed to the children and young persons
- Practical and other relevant services to the children and young persons and their families
sections.Who is this for?: Children and young persons who face abuse or neglect at home.
sections.How to apply?:
- Referral is required.
- Contact CPSC via phone call or email to enquire on the referral process.
sections.What to expect?:
- After receiving the referral, the social worker from CPSC will contact the referring person to find out more about the presenting abuse or neglect concerns.
- The CPSC will then inform on whether the referral is assessed to be suitable for CPSC to provide the intervention.
- If assessed to not be suitable, CPSC will advise on the other possible services or contact points.

title: Family Service Centre (FSC)
description: FSCs provide support for vulnerable individuals and families with social and emotional issues, and work towards stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

sections.About this support:
FSCs are community-based social services that provide support for vulnerable individuals and families with social and emotional issues. Social Work Practitioners at the FSCs provide case management support and also partner with other agencies to coordinate holistic support for clients to help them achieve stability, self-reliance, and social mobility.

FSC services include:

- Information and Referral: Providing information about social services, and linking individuals and families to appropriate social services and community resources based on the assessed needs
- Casework: Providing holistic case management and individual/family counselling
- Group Work: Bringing individuals and families with common needs together for purposeful group interactions to address their concerns and bring about positive change
- Community Work: Tapping on community resources to help individuals and families support and empower one another.
sections.Who is this for?:
FSCs are open to families and individuals:

- Regardless of age, race, language or religion;
- At different life stages (such as couples, families with young children, adolescents, or elderly members); and
- Of various family structures
sections.How to apply?:
Call, walk in or email the FSCs for help on family, socio-emotional, interpersonal or other social issues. 
To find the FSC in your neighbourhood, you can call ComCare hotline at [1800 222 0000](tel:18002220000) or visit 
https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories.
sections.What to expect?:
- Upon contact with a FSC, a FSC worker will assess the needs of the individual/family and determine the type of support needed.
- If FSC services are required, the FSC will then work with the individual/family on their issues with the appropriate social work interventions.
- If the FSC’s services are not required and other supportive services by other partners can help to meet these needs, the FSC worker will refer the individual/family to appropriate social services or community resources.
